title: New artifact IPC commands bypass the shared channel contract

evidence.quote: rule: privileged renderer-to-main channels must be declared in a shared contract and preload may expose only handled methods

evidence.note: Today's copy, timestamp, repository-classification and Trash methods repeat channel literals.
Channel inventory resides in Electron main implementation; preload does not consume it.
Shared command registry omits today's four artifact commands.
Registration parity checks main-owned inventory only; preload side is outside check.

observed: Today's four artifact IPC commands each have a live main handler and preload caller, but their channel names are duplicated literals instead of being declared and consumed from the shared IPC contract.
expected_boundary: Active ARC-003 requires privileged renderer-to-main channels to be declared in a shared contract.
failure_mechanism: The new features extended the implementation-owned FILE_IPC_CHANNELS list and preload literals while bypassing ipc/channels.ts. Main-side registration tests cannot enforce producer/consumer channel parity.
break_it_angle: Compare the producer, receiving handler, shared registry and registration test rather than treating a main-only channel inventory as a shared contract.
impact: Confirmed architectural invariant drift with a missing compile-time rename boundary. No current channel mismatch, privilege defect, or runtime failure is claimed.

mitigation.minimal_repair: Declare the four newly added command names in ipc/channels.ts and consume those constants in preload, main registration and FILE_IPC_CHANNELS.
mitigation.local_guardrail: Keep the shared contract import renderer-safe; no Electron main implementation imports in preload.
mitigation.behavior_test: Exercise the actual preload methods against a stub IPC bridge and verify each selected channel resolves to its registered main handler.

implementation_assessment.rationale: A bounded constant extraction across existing main/preload/contract files preserves the existing payload and runtime behavior.

validation: Static comparison confirms all four current handlers exist and match the caller literals.
After repair run targeted file IPC/preload tests and Desktop typecheck; no runtime behavior change expected.
non_goals: No security audit or access-policy changes.
Do not sweep older IPC literals or redesign the whole IPC layer.

confidence_calibration.rationale: Explicit active invariant versus quoted implementation; current behavior is matched, impact is governance and drift resistance only.

title: Directory mutation response omits updated workspace folder policy

evidence.note: Baseline a48108750: mutation applies path list only.
Baseline a48108750: added roots absent from metadata select generic Workspace policy label.
Baseline: backend saves extended policy while response contains only directory lists.
Baseline SessionWorkingDirsResponse contains no policy-root projection.

observed: Adding a directory to an active workspace session persists its effective folder policy but returns and applies only the directory paths. The new directory is listed immediately with a generic Workspace policy label until a full session reload.
expected_boundary: Core owns canonical workspace policy, and Desktop presents its current response metadata rather than independently inferring policy.
failure_mechanism: The new access-label consumer was wired to full session metadata without extending the existing mutation response and adapter.
break_it_angle: Trace add-directory through backend context write, typed response, Desktop adapter and rendered label before any full session reload.
impact: Low-impact stale access display for the newly granted folder; actual access policy and existing read-only roots are unchanged.

mitigation.minimal_repair: Include effective workspace roots in the directory mutation response and propagate them through adapter and component state, preserving old-server fallback.
mitigation.local_guardrail: Reuse canonical WorkspaceFolderPolicyRoot; keep existing policy/persistence and extension-refresh rollback unchanged.
mitigation.behavior_test: After adding a workspace directory, render updated state without reload and assert Read/write/run rather than Workspace policy; retain read-only overlap labels.

implementation_assessment.rationale: Small metadata addition crosses Rust DTO/generated SDK and existing Desktop adapter; no new permission behavior or persistence.

validation: Static baseline producer/consumer trace proves omitted policy projection.
Regression tests should cover new grant response, old-server omission, existing read-only roots and immediate rendered label.
non_goals: No workspace mutation/removal or default-session changes.

confidence_calibration.rationale: Deterministic omitted metadata and fallback label; no race or permission effect claimed.
